page: Microsoft Azure D32nlds_v6 is a virtual machine within the Dnldv6 series powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system provides 32 dedicated vCPUs based on x86_64 Intel processor architecture alongside 64.0 GB of memory, delivering a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates without hardware acceleration, featuring zero graphics processing units.

For high-throughput scratch space, the instance includes 1888 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage volumes for external disk attachments. The instance profile is classified as network optimized, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

By combining 32 dedicated cores with a modest 64.0 GB RAM footprint, the configuration reduces memory-related overhead for workloads driven by processor concurrency and high local I/O performance rather than expansive in-memory state. Optimal application scenarios include CI/CD build environments, batch processing, static web serving clusters, and data processing nodes requiring low-latency NVMe temporary caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D32nlds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual instance powered by dedicated Intel processors on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Featuring 32 vCPUs alongside 64.0 GB of system memory, the machine delivers a lean 2.0 GB of RAM per core allocation suited for compute-focused operations that do not require dense memory arrays. A notable hardware component is its integrated 1888 GB NVMe SSD local storage volume, complemented by Premium Storage capability for external disks. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not supply complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because memory capacity is constrained relative to core count, the D32nlds_v6 offers strong hardware efficiency for workloads prioritizing raw compute concurrency and high-throughput temporary storage over memory residency. Suitable application scenarios include continuous integration and deployment pipelines, video or batch data processing, network services, and distributed database systems requiring fast local scratch disks.
